subject: Post-call: RTBF / deletion workflow & backup timelines
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@insurely.com>, Tom Beckett <t.beckett@insurely.com>
Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-09T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: RTBF / deletion workflow & backup timelines

Hi Sarah / Tom —

Thanks again for taking the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps on the RTBF/deletion items we discussed so you can share with legal/compliance: 

Summary of what we discussed
- Logical delete: when a user requests deletion, Redwood will immediately mark records for deletion and remove access from the product surface (effective immediately).
- Primary storage purge: primary DB objects are scheduled for cryptographic deletion within 30 days after the request is processed.
- Backups & snapshots: snapshots are immutable for a retention window; our standard is 90 days for backups. We can accelerate rotation for enterprise customers with a contractual change but cannot guarantee immediate removal from existing immutable backups unless a shorter retention policy is agreed and applied going forward.
- Logs & telemetry: operational logs (error/ingest traces) are retained for 90 days by default; access is restricted and audit logged. We can scope what telemetry is stored per contract (PII-stripping options).
- Data residency: data for Insurely can be pinned to the AWS us-west-2 region; cross-region replication can be turned off for compliance.
- Key management: customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) supported for Private deployments; in hosted mode we offer Bring-Your-Own-Key for dedicated contracts.

Open items / clarifications requested from your side
1) Can you confirm whether contractually you need backup purge <90 days, or whether 90-day rotation is acceptable?
2) Are there any legal holds / litigation holds we need to be aware of for a subset of users?
3) Which team should be the sign-off contact for a mutual action plan (legal, security, or ops)?

Attachments: redwood-rtbf-sla.pdf (SLA + deletion timeline), delete-process-diagram.png

Next steps
- I can set up a 30-min technical + compliance follow-up next week to walk through the proposed MAP and timeline. Please propose 2 windows.
- If you confirm you need <90-day backup deletion, we’ll have to route to product + legal to scope (should be possible with a contractual amendment).

Thanks —
Camila Reyes
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
camila@redwood.com | (415) 555-0192

From: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@insurely.com>

Date: 2026-05-09T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: RTBF / deletion workflow & backup timelines

Hi Camila —

Thanks for the clear recap. A few quick clarifying questions from our side before we loop legal: 

1) Backups: We have a customer requirement that certain PII must be purged from backups within 30 days of a subject access request. Is there a technical path for a one-time purge of existing backups for a targeted tenant if we sign an addendum? If not, is there an alternative mitigation you offer (e.g., crypto-delete via key rotation)?

2) Logs: We noted you retain telemetry for 90 days. Can you confirm whether those logs may contain PII or user-identifiers that would be considered personal data under GDPR? If so, can those be redacted at ingestion for our tenant?

3) Audit trail: For compliance we need an immutable audit showing the lifecycle of the deletion request (received, processed, primary purge, backup retention expiration). Is that something you can provide as a report or API?

4) Cutover timeline: If we go forward, we need a mutual action plan and an explicit timeline for the deletion SLA. Who should we expect to work that with us on Redwood’s side?

Happy to join the technical follow-up. Prefer Tue/Wed next week 2–4pm PT.

Best,
Sarah Lin
Head of Security & Privacy, Insurely
sarah.lin@insurely.com

From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@insurely.com>, Tom Beckett <t.beckett@insurely.com>
Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-09T11:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: RTBF / deletion workflow & backup timelines

Hi Sarah — thanks for the questions. Mateo (our product lead on data controls) and I put together answers below; happy to walk through on a call.

1) Backup purge path: Short answer — we cannot reliably modify immutable historical backups already written to WORM-style snapshots to surgically remove a tenant’s records, except in limited on-prem cases. Options: 
  - Contractual/operational approach: shorten the backup retention window going forward (e.g., to 30 days) and agree an exception that new backups will be rotated faster for Insurely. This does not retroactively remove data from prior backups.
  - Crypto-delete via key rotation: for Dedicated/Private deployments where customer manages keys, rotating/destroying the encryption key for a backup snapshot can render the backups unreadable. For hosted/shared keys, this is not available without a contract and migration to a BYOK/dedicated key model.

2) Logs and PII: Our standard ingestion pipeline strips user-provided PII from telemetry for production customers by default; however some operational IDs (hashed user IDs, request IDs) are retained for debugging. We can enable a stricter ingestion pipeline for Insurely that redacts or hashes additional fields before storage. We’ll need a short mapping doc from your side that lists fields you consider PII.

3) Audit trail: Yes — we can provide an audit report per deletion request showing timestamps for request received, request processed, primary object purge, and retention-expiry date for backups. The audit can be exported as CSV or via an API endpoint on Redwood Console (we’ll include a sample schema).

4) MAP / contacts:
  - Redwood side: Camila (AE) + Mateo (Product, data controls) + an engineer from Reliability for the tech deep-dive. Legal will join if we need contractual changes.
  - Suggested process: 1) Technical deep-dive to confirm the ingestion/logging mapping (30min). 2) Draft MAP and upstream to legal if shorter backup retention is required. 3) Sign amendment and schedule cutover.

Proposed follow-up windows: Tue 2026-05-12 14:00 PT or Wed 2026-05-13 15:00 PT. Which works for you?

Regards,
Camila Reyes
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
